item.content:encoded:
I will agree with you on your points (since in high-tech Asian economic hubs, the norm is to work wherever and whenever possible). I've known many adults who work overtime as the "default working hours" (they could really do a 9 to 5, but more hours more cash).

Given the Foundation's ultra-high stress job scope that may shatter one's worldview, I would say SCP-765 is more of a measure for those personnel who are so overworked but cannot (or not willing) to take a break. I mean, knowing that the world could fuck over in so many ways tends to do a number on a sane mind.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It doesn't have to be something anomalous or spooky, even. In the USA, especially in corporate or high-pressure positions, there's an implicit assumption that you're never really off the clock. People take their phones and laptops with them when they're "on vacation" and do work or check their email or whatever. And that's assuming that people take vacation at all; workers in the USA are some of the least likely in the world to use all the time off they've accrued, both due to a culture of overwork and a fear of being fired/not promoted/etc. if they're not seen "giving it their all".

Again, all that above is as things currently actually exist in the real world in the USA. Now imagine that this is the Foundation, where researchers/agents are under tremendously greater stresses and pressures. The same people who, in the real world, are likely to keep working because they feel like they have to are going to be even MORE SO as members of the Foundation.

So yeah. Depressing as it is, this is more a matter of the Foundation trying to side-step workaholism and burnout without having the sufferers of such resist.quack

Yeah, see how the article doesn't state anything about justification for murder? There isn't even a tiny hint/trace of this thing doing more than making people feel good.

One again, the article itself is boring and uninteresting because it needs outside theories to make it more than a feel-good pond with ducks. I'm not saying it needs to be grimdark at all to be interesting, it could be interesting without any horror being implied, but this isn't it.

If an article needs speculation to be even remotely interesting then it's doing something wrong.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It's not just relaxing. It puts a compulsion on you that makes you feel good about all your past decisions as well, washing away guilt and pain.

Think about that for a while. It's an incredibly dangerous effect, but it's completely understated in the article.

There are way too many things on the site that beats you in the head with every dark and twisted implication and completely kills any level of subtlety there might have been, and far too few things where you really have to sit back and let the horror soak into you.

I mean, we could grimdark it up and say it was discovered after noticing an increase in domestic violence in the area and theorized its existence after reviewing interviews with a local serial killer that stated that while he would feel guilty after killing someone, one trip down to his old fishing hole and he'd feel better about what he was doing right away. (It would be a pretty horrible addition though.)

That just reinforces how bland this thing is. Without outside guessing on who gets assigned to it it's just a duck pond, it serves the same purpose as a vacation for people who work on shitty SCPs (not shitty in quality.)

All of that aside, look at it, it's a peaceful pond that makes people feel better because it's relaxing. How was it discovered? Who came across it and was so utterly shaken with it's niceness that they decided it must be beyond the constraints of normalcy?

"Oh man, I'm so depressed and I hate my job…. This is a nice duck pond, it's so calming and relaxing… I can just feel my troubles melting away… Wait… No…. NO NO NO! It's too relaxing! I have to call the cops! Oh jeez, this is going to change the world!"

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Not everything has to be flashy and world shaking.

You've also not thought through the consequences.

Dr ██████ is in charge of arranging feedings for SCP-974, but the last batch…. The child selected looked just like his kid brother. My God, what are we doing? We're monsters. How the hell did I end up like this? I'd do anything to take it all back. Now they station me out here as punishment because they must know what I'm thinking about. What's the point?

Though I guess if I think about it; It's distasteful, but we have to do it. The Foundation is doing good work, even if we do have to make sad choices. I'm so glad I work here. It's so peaceful out here watching those ducks on the pond. Sure my wife left me, but I had to be dedicated to my work. There's nothing I would change. I regret nothing. It all had to be done.
